sections.h2: Where do Lewis County, Kentucky owners go about a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Two offices share one address in Vanceburg. Both sit at 112 Second Street, one in Suite 101 and the other in Suite 102, which makes it easy to settle a question about value and a question about payment in the same trip.

Lewis County tax offices in Vanceburg
OfficeWhat it doesLocationPhone
Property Valuation AdministratorAppraises real property, handles exemptions and address changes112 Second Street, Suite 101606-796-2622
Lewis County SheriffMails and collects the current-year bill for the state, county and school districts112 Second Street, Suite 102606-796-2912
Lewis County ClerkTakes over delinquent bills and hosts the appeal filingVanceburg, the county seatListed on the clerk's website

Some bills also carry charges for fire protection or library districts, which the sheriff collects too. The PVA's office page stresses what it does not do: it writes no laws and sets no rates. Those belong to the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, and the PVA only assigns value. Under state rules the office walks every parcel at least once each four years, and since 1992 it may measure the outside of a building with no one home.

sections.h2: What is Lewis County like beyond the tax office?
sections.html:
Up in Kentucky's northeast, Lewis County follows the Ohio River for more miles than any other county in the state. Across the water are Adams and Scioto counties in Ohio, and Greenup, Carter, Rowan, Fleming and Mason counties fill in the Kentucky side. Elevation climbs from 485 feet to 1,400, and oak cut from its wooded hills once ranked among the nation's best lumber.

Mason County gave up the land on December 2, 1806, and the new county took the name of the explorer Meriwether Lewis. The seat has moved twice: Poplar Flat held it first, Clarksburg from 1809 to 1863, and Vanceburg since. Vanceburg and Concord are the only cities, Garrison is the one census-designated place, and Tollesboro, Kinniconick and Laurel are among the many small communities. The 2020 count placed all residents in rural territory.

One school district serves the county, with four elementaries, in Vanceburg, Garrison, Tollesboro and Laurel, plus a middle school and a high school beside KY 10, the AA Highway. Tollesboro's own high school closed in 1994, a closure that stirred real controversy at the time. The county profile counts 814 jobs in health care and social assistance, 680 in construction and 600 in manufacturing, so lumber is no longer the lead.

  • Mean travel time to work: 38.6 minutes.
  • A typical owned home is worth $96,000, and 79.2 percent of homes are lived in by their owners.
  • Median rent: $751, and median household income: $46,838.
  • Headcount estimated at 12,901 in mid-2025, off 1.4 percent from the 2020 base.

sections.h2: How does the Lewis County sheriff want the bill paid?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page gives three routes. Mail the stub and a check to 112 Second Street, Suite 102, Vanceburg, KY 41179, pay in person at the office, or pay by debit or credit card over the phone or at the counter. Card payments add a fee tied to the bill's amount. Make checks out to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office, write the property ID from the bill on the check, and never mail cash.

Pay only the single figure in the "If Paid By" box at the bottom right of the bill. The subtotals for each taxing jurisdiction are shown for information, and separate payments for each would only cause confusion. A bounced check draws a $25 charge, and the late-payment tiers keep running while you replace it. If you overpaid, phone the sheriff, who may ask for paperwork before refunding. A single payment can cover several parcels as long as each stub is enclosed.

Statute sets the calendar. The state ladder is simple: a 2 percent reward for settling early in the fall, no adjustment during the last two months of the year, then a 5 percent charge in January and 10 percent beyond that. Your own statement prints the exact dollar figure for each window, so trust it over any summary.

sections.h2: What happens when a Lewis County tax bill goes unpaid past April?
sections.html:
Mid-April is the handoff. Whatever the sheriff has not collected by then goes to the clerk as a certificate of delinquency, with a lien recorded against the house. After that the debt grows by a percent each month, plus commissions for the clerk and the county attorney.

The state's own illustration starts with a $1,000 bill. Clear it within five business days of the handoff and the total is $1,387.79, with the attorney's cut waived. Let the first attorney letter go out and it becomes $1,611.30. Investors can buy these debts at a clerk's sale, which in a usual year lands somewhere between July 14 and August 28.

One exception to the calendar: a bill covering property missing from the roll, or a value that went up on appeal, is payable the day it is drafted, and another 10 percent attaches after a month of silence.

sections.h2: How can I contest a Lewis County valuation?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA's staff for a face-to-face review first. No appeal is accepted without one, and it has to be held ahead of or during the public viewing period.

Viewing runs thirteen days from the opening Monday of May. Having met with the PVA, you can lodge the appeal at the clerk's office until the following workday ends. State law seats the review panel in the county seat, which puts Lewis County hearings in Vanceburg about four to five weeks after viewing wraps up.

  • The board hears only evidence presented with both you and the PVA present, so plan to attend or send an authorized representative.
  • Useful evidence includes photos, insurance policies, construction costs, an appraisal, and nearby listings or sales.
  • Audio recording is your right. The PVA may record only if it gives you written notice.
  • Skipping the board forfeits any later appeal to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Lewis County homestead exemption?
sections.html:
The break is for people who live in the house and are either 65 or older or rated totally disabled. The statewide figure for assessment years 2025 and 2026 is $49,100, subtracted from the assessed value before any rate is multiplied.

The sheriff's page points applicants to the PVA at 606-796-2622. A household gets one, even when both spouses qualify, and a manufactured house or a mobile home taxed as real estate can serve as the residence. After a sale the buyer files fresh, and the seller tells the PVA that title has moved.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when a Lewis County house sells?
sections.html:
According to the sheriff, sellers typically cover a share at the closing table that matches their months of ownership, and the buyer writes the check for the whole bill when it comes. The closing paperwork shows how your deal split it. A mortgage servicer that pays from escrow still lets the owner see the bill, and the owner stays legally responsible for it.

The bill is sent to whoever owned the property on January 1, unless a deed filed afterward carries specific tax bill instructions for the current year. Recording the deed also triggers Kentucky's transfer levy under KRS 142.050, half a dollar for each $500 of price, which the clerk collects. Foreclosures, divorce settlements and gifts from parent to child are among the exemptions. If a tax bill is delinquent, expect the title agent to require a payoff from the sheriff or the clerk before funds are released.

faqs.q: Which phone line answers Lewis County tax questions?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff at 606-796-2912 about payment, and the PVA at 606-796-2622 about value or exemptions. Both offices are at 112 Second Street in Vanceburg.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Lewis County tax with a card?
faqs.a: Yes. The sheriff takes debit and credit cards over the phone or at the office and charges a convenience fee based on the bill's size. Checks go to the Lewis County Sheriff's Office with the property ID written on them.

faqs.q: What does a bounced check cost in Lewis County?
faqs.a: The fee is $25, and the late-payment schedule printed on the bill still applies when you send a replacement payment. Pay the amount for the date your funds actually arrive.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage lender handle the Lewis County bill?
faqs.a: Often, but you still receive a copy and remain legally responsible. If you think escrow covers it and you are unsure, ask the lender, and ask the sheriff if the bill is missing.

faqs.q: Who covers the tax when a Lewis County house is sold?
faqs.a: The settlement statement decides, and sellers usually cover a prorated share for the months they owned the house. The buyer pays the full bill when it comes, and unpaid back taxes must be cleared before the title is clean.
